question: The power consumption of an electrical device varies directly with the square of the voltage applied. If a device consumes 150 watts when the voltage is 120 volts, how much power (in watts) will it consume at 240 volts?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Power varies directly with the square of the voltage: P ∝ V²

Since the voltage is doubled (from 120 V to 240 V), the power consumed will be multiplied by 2² = 4.

New Power = 150 × 4 = 600 watts.

**∴ The correct answer is 600 watts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Power (P₁) = 150 W

Initial Voltage (V₁) = 120 V

Final Voltage (V₂) = 240 V

**Formula Used:**

P ∝ V² ⇒ P₁ / V₁² = P₂ / V₂²

 
 Initial State
 V1 = 120 V
 P1 = 150 W
 
 

 

 Voltage × 2
 Power × 22
 
 
 Final State
 V2 = 240 V
 P2 = ?
 
 
 P2 = 150 × 4 = 600 W

**Calculations:**

⇒ 150 / 120² = P₂ / 240²

⇒ P₂ = 150 × (240 / 120)²

⇒ P₂ = 150 × (2)²

⇒ P₂ = 150 × 4

⇒ P₂ = 600

**∴ The correct answer is 600 watts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

When two quantities vary directly, an increase in one causes a proportional increase in the other. Formula: A = kB

Inverse Variation

When two quantities vary inversely, an increase in one causes a proportional decrease in the other. Formula: A = k / B

Joint Variation

When a quantity varies directly as the product of two or more other quantities. Formula: A = kBC
